meta.title: Persian C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Persian → English (see the Persian, recall the meaning) and English → Persian (see an English meaning, recall the Persian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. The Persian taught is the standard written language of Iran (Farsi), with the everyday spoken form shown beside a word where Tehran speech says it differently. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Persian, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 63 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — philosophy and ethics, religion, mysticism and the inner life, scholarly Persian, government and the constitution, the economy and development, medicine and the body, law and rights, language and the forms of Persian poetry, the shades of feeling and judgement, the abstract nouns and adjectives of formal prose, and the literary connectors — and the other 1437 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Persian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb, and its spoken form, added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in the Persian script with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's Iranian one (â for the long a, x for kh, š for sh: ketâb, xâne), since the script writes no short vowels; the Persian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. The 1105 nouns show their plural; the 27 verbs show their present stem, which no rule derives from the infinitive and on which every present tense is built, and behind the All forms fold their present, past, future, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 424 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 69 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
